mainTopic: Did בית שמאי practice their own rulings, and how does that fit with לא תתגודדו?
overview: This amud asks whether בית שמאי actually lived by their own rulings against בית הלל, or only argued in the study hall. ריש לקיש and רב say they did not act on them, while רבי יוחנן and שמואל say they certainly did. The גמרא explains both views twice. The first explanation places the dispute before the בת קול, where the question is whether the majority of בית הלל binds sharper opponents. The second places it after the בת קול, where the 'did act' side follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a heavenly voice. The 'did act' view seems to clash with לא תתגודדו, the ban on splitting into groups. אביי limits that ban to two courts in one city, and רבא limits it further to one court split in half. Stories about different towns practicing differently, even on שבת, and about רבי אבהו moving a lamp in one town but not another, are shown to fit these rules. Finally, the משנה says the two schools still married each other. The גמרא explains that בית שמאי did act on their view but warned בית הלל about problem families, and the משנה's clause about purity supports this.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: בית שמאי did not actually practice their view
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that בית שמאי never actually acted on their opinion. The disagreement stayed theoretical.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think בית שמאי acted according to their own words? בית שמאי did not act according to their words.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש is answering רבי יוחנן. He rejects the idea that בית שמאי actually practiced their opinion in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had pointed to בית שמאי and בית הלל to show that different groups may practice differently. ריש לקיש answers that this proves nothing, because בית שמאי never actually practiced their view. Their disagreement stayed in learning, not in action.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really think? (a way of pushing back)
They acted, meaning they practiced it in real life
According to their own words or ruling
The school of שמאי, which usually argues with בית הלל

steps.confusionAlert: Holding an opinion is not the same as acting on it. The question here is not who was right. It is whether בית שמאי actually did what they said.

phrases.english: Do you really think
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is the one speaking here, and he is talking to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: that Beit Shammai acted according to their words?
Beit Shammai did not act according to their words.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ עָשׂוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי כְּדִבְרֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation from before this section, pushing back on its assumption.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that בית שמאי's view was ever put into practice.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes that a debate in learning means people actually acted differently.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: They certainly did act
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds the opposite. בית שמאי really did practice their own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: they certainly did act.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן states his position against ריש לקיש. בית שמאי really lived by their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word עשו ועשו adds strength: 'they surely did.' Now there are two clear opposing views on what actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: They certainly acted (the doubling makes it strong)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: they certainly did act.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to ריש לקיש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי did practice their own opinion.

steps.title: The same dispute between רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב and שמואל argue about the very same question. רב matches ריש לקיש, and שמואל matches רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also argued by רב and שמואל. רב says בית שמאי did not act on their words, and שמואל says they certainly did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that this argument also exists in בבל, between רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is decided here. The גמרא simply shows that both sides have major supporters. רב lines up with ריש לקיש (did not act), and שמואל lines up with רבי יוחנן (did act).

phrases.english: And this is the dispute of Rav and Shmuel.
For Rav says: they did not act
— Beit Shammai — according to their words,
and Shmuel says: they certainly did act.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the same argument from steps 1-2 among other אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: they did not act. שמואל: they did act.
steps.whatToRemember: Did not act: ריש לקיש and רב. Did act: רבי יוחנן and שמואל.

steps.title: When? Each time period makes one side hard to explain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which time period is being discussed. Before the בת קול, the 'did not act' view is hard to explain. After the בת קול, the 'did act' view is hard to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was this? If before the בת קול, what is the reason of the one who says they did not act? But if after the בת קול, what is the reason of the one who says they did act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks like it is asking a simple question about time. Really it is a challenge, because each choice seems to make one side make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the בת קול, the law was not yet decided, so why would בית שמאי hold back from their own view? After the בת קול declared the law like בית הלל, how could בית שמאי go against it? Either way, one opinion seems to fall apart.

phrases.english: When?
If you say before the heavenly voice —

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר לֹא עָשׂוּ?
phrases.english: what is the reason of the one who says they did not act?
But rather after the heavenly voice —
what is the reason of the one who says they did act?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא קוֹדֶם בַּת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the dispute from steps 1-3 by asking which time period it refers to.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before the בת קול, there seems no reason to hold back. After it, there seems no right to act against it. So each time period knocks out one view.

steps.title: Either time period can work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the dispute could be about before the בת קול or about after it. It will explain both.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it was before the בת קול. And if you want, say it was after the בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא says both choices can work, and next it will explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of picking one time period, the גמרא says either one can be defended. Steps 6-7 explain the 'before' option, and step 8 explains the 'after' option.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קוֹדֶם בַּת קוֹל,
phrases.english: If you want, say before the heavenly voice,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא לְאַחַר בַּת קוֹל.
phrases.english: and if you want, say after the heavenly voice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קוֹדֶם בַּת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two possible answers, each one defended in turn.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each time period knocks out one side.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both time periods can be explained.

steps.title: Before the heavenly voice: בית הלל were the majority
steps.stepSummary: Before the בת קול, בית הלל had more people. So the one who says בית שמאי did not act relies on the rule of following the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it was before the בת קול, at a time when בית הלל were the majority. The one who says they did not act reasons that בית הלל were the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the 'did not act' view for the time before the בת קול. בית שמאי held back because בית הלל had the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge asked why anyone would hold back before the law was decided. The answer: it was in a sense already decided, because the majority, בית הלל, sets the law. So בית שמאי gave in to the majority in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: And for example, in a case where

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קוֹדֶם בַּת קוֹל,
phrases.english: If you want, say before the heavenly voice,
and in a case where Beit Hillel are the majority,
according to the one who says they did not act —
it is because Beit Hillel are the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קוֹדֶם בַּת קוֹל, וּכְגוֹן דְּבֵית הִלֵּל רוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first option offered in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a detail about the case: בית הלל were the majority.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Before the בת קול, there was no reason for בית שמאי to hold back.
steps.terutzMaskana: The majority rule already decided the law, so בית שמאי held back.

steps.title: Why some say they did act: בית שמאי were sharper
steps.stepSummary: The one who says בית שמאי did act holds that we only follow the majority between equals. בית שמאי were sharper, so the majority rule did not bind them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says they did act holds: we follow the majority only when the two sides are equal. Here, בית שמאי were sharper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the 'did act' view handles the majority problem. Following the majority only works when both sides are equally wise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view limits the majority rule: it decides only between equals. Since בית שמאי were sharper thinkers, their smaller number did not cancel their view. So they could practice their own opinion.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say בית שמאי were not a minority. It says that, according to this view, being a minority did not decide the law, because the sides were not equal in sharpness.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule of following the majority can depend on the two sides being equal in wisdom.
steps.whatToRemember: Before the בת קול: 'did not act' = majority rules. 'Did act' = majority rules only between equals, and בית שמאי were sharper.

phrases.english: And the one who says they did act,
when do we follow the majority? —
where they are equal to each other.
Here, Beit Shammai are sharper.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר עָשׂוּ, כִּי אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reasoning for the same 'before' period from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the majority rule to cases where both sides are equal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The majority of בית הלל should have stopped בית שמאי from acting.
steps.terutzMaskana: Majority rules only between equals, and בית שמאי were sharper, so they acted on their view.

steps.title: Second explanation: the dispute is about after the heavenly voice
steps.stepSummary: If the dispute is about after the בת קול, the 'did not act' view relies on the בת קול, and the 'did act' view follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say the dispute is about the time after the בת קול. The one who says בית שמאי did not act holds so because the בת קול had already come out. The one who says they did act follows רבי יהושע, who said we do not pay attention to a בת קול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its second answer, explaining the dispute if it is about the time after the בת קול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 4, the problem was that after the בת קול it is hard to see how anyone could say בית שמאי acted. The answer: רבי יהושע held that a בת קול does not decide הלכה. So the 'did act' view can stand even after the בת קול came out.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces a second possible answer
We do not pay attention to it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע did not say the בת קול was false. He said הלכה is decided by the חכמים here on earth, not by a voice from heaven.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא לְאַחַר בַּת קוֹל,
phrases.english: And if you want, say it is about after the heavenly voice:
the one who says they did not act
holds so because the heavenly voice had already come out.
And the one who says they did act
follows the view of רבי יהושע,
who said: we do not pay attention to a heavenly voice.
phrases.notes: He said this in the story of the oven of עכנאי, in בבא מציעא 59b.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא לְאַחַר בַּת קוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second option promised in step 5, after steps 6-7 explained the 'before the בת קול' option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties each side to a known opinion about whether a בת קול counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After the בת קול, nobody could say בית שמאי acted on their view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'did act' view follows רבי יהושע, who ignores a בת קול.

steps.title: Challenge: acting differently breaks the rule against splitting into groups
steps.stepSummary: If בית שמאי acted on their own view, that seems to break the פסוק 'לא תתגודדו', which teaches not to split into separate groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says they did act, we should apply here 'לא תתגודדו', which means: do not become separate groups!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'did act' view with a rule from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the majority rule or the בת קול did not stop בית שמאי, there is another problem. If one group follows בית שמאי and another follows בית הלל, the Jewish people become split. The פסוק לא תתגודדו is read as a ban on that.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not cut yourselves (דברים 14:1), read here as: do not split into groups
We should apply this פסוק here

phrases.english: And according to the one who says they did act,
we should apply here "Do not cut yourselves":
do not become separate groups!
phrases.notes: The word תתגודדו sounds like אגודה, a group, so the פסוק is also read this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דַּאֲמַר עָשׂוּ, קָרֵינַן כָּאן לֹא תִתְגּוֹדְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'did act' view that steps 7 and 8 defended.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that בית שמאי acted on their own rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two groups following different rulings creates the splitting forbidden by לא תתגודדו.

steps.title: אביי: the ban only applies to two courts in one city
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that לא תתגודדו only applies when two courts in the same city rule differently. Courts in two different cities are fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: לא תתגודדו applies when there are two courts in one city, one ruling like בית שמאי and the other like בית הלל. But two courts in two different cities is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by limiting when לא תתגודדו applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the problem is only when two rulings exist side by side in one city. If each city follows its own court, nobody is split. So בית שמאי could act on their view in their own places.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no problem with it

phrases.english: אביי said:
When we say "Do not cut yourselves,"

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שְׁתֵּי בָּתֵּי דִינִים בְּעִיר אַחַת,
phrases.english: it is for a case like two courts in one city,
these rule like the words of בית שמאי,
and those rule like the words of בית הלל.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁתֵּי בָּתֵּי דִינִים בִּשְׁתֵּי עֲיָירוֹת
phrases.english: But two courts in two cities,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי אָמְרִינַן לֹא תִתְגּוֹדְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case where the rule applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any difference in practice breaks לא תתגודדו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only two courts in one city break it; separate cities are fine.

steps.title: רבא: בית שמאי and בית הלל were like two courts in one city
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes back: בית שמאי and בית הלל were exactly like two courts in the same city, so אביי's answer does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But בית שמאי and בית הלל are like two courts in one city!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי allowed different rulings only in different cities. But בית שמאי and בית הלל were not split by town; they lived and ruled side by side. So by אביי's own rule, the problem of לא תתגודדו comes right back.

phrases.english: רבא said to him:
But בית שמאי and בית הלל

phrases.aramaic: כִּשְׁתֵּי בָּתֵּי דִינִים בְּעִיר אַחַת דָּמֵי!
phrases.english: are like two courts in one city!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's answer as applied to בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בית שמאי and בית הלל were not in separate cities, so they fit the forbidden case.

steps.title: רבא: the ban only applies to one court split in half
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that לא תתגודדו applies only when a single court splits, half ruling one way and half the other. Two separate courts, even in one city, are fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: לא תתגודדו applies when one court in one city is split, half ruling like בית שמאי and half like בית הלל. But two courts in one city is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the challenge of לא תתגודדו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא moves the line further than אביי. The problem is only when one single court gives two different rulings. Two separate courts, like בית שמאי and בית הלל, may each rule their way even in the same city, so the 'did act' view is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous answer and gives a new one
They rule, they teach the הלכה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, לא תתגודדו only forbids one court splitting itself in two. Separate courts may follow different views, so בית שמאי could act on their rulings.

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
When we say "Do not cut yourselves,"
it is for a case like a court in one city,
half of which rules like the words of בית שמאי,
and half rules like the words of בית הלל.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שְׁתֵּי בָּתֵּי דִינִין בְּעִיר אַחַת
phrases.english: But two courts in one city,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כִּי אָמְרִינַן לֹא תִתְגּוֹדְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new answer to step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the forbidden case even further than אביי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two courts in one city break לא תתגודדו (אביי's view).
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one court split in half breaks it; two courts in one city are fine.

steps.title: Source: towns followed their own local רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a source: in רבי אליעזר's town they cut wood on שבת to make a מילה knife, and in רבי יוסי הגלילי's town they ate poultry with milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In the place of רבי אליעזר, they would cut wood on שבת to make charcoal to make iron. In the place of רבי יוסי הגלילי, they would eat poultry with milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about real practice, opening a new look at whether people acted on a view that was not the accepted הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are two cases where a תנא's own view was followed in his town, even though most חכמים disagreed. The source is brought as a challenge: if people in different places practiced differently, even on שבת, that seems to be the splitting forbidden by לא תתגודדו.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place, in the town where he was the רב

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In the place of רבי אליעזר
they would cut wood to make charcoal
on שבת, to make iron.
phrases.notes: The iron is the knife for a ברית מילה on שבת; רבי אליעזר held even preparing it pushes aside שבת.

phrases.english: In the place of רבי יוסי הגלילי
they would eat poultry meat with milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining לא תתגודדו, the גמרא brings a source that seems to challenge it: different towns practiced differently on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a group may act on its own view against the majority
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source reporting that the towns of רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי הגלילי followed their local רב's rulings
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of לא תתגודדו as defined in steps 10-12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different towns followed different rulings on serious שבת matters, which seems to be forbidden splitting into groups.

steps.title: Only in רבי אליעזר's town, not in רבי עקיבא's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the source closely: they cut wood for a מילה knife only in רבי אליעזר's town. In רבי עקיבא's town they did not, because רבי עקיבא taught that anything that could be done before שבת does not push aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רבי אליעזר's place, yes. In רבי עקיבא's place, no. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי עקיבא stated a general rule: any forbidden work that could have been done on ערב שבת does not push aside שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the source in step 13. It points out that the practice happened only in רבי אליעזר's town, while רבי עקיבא's town acted differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the knife could have been done before שבת, so רבי עקיבא would forbid it. This means two places really acted differently on a שבת question. That seems to touch the issue of לא תתגודדו.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place, meaning the town where that rabbi was the authority
Pushes aside שבת, meaning it is allowed even though it is normally forbidden

phrases.english: In the place of Rabbi Eliezer, yes;
in the place of Rabbi Akiva, no.
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Akiva stated a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: Any forbidden work that could be done on ערב שבת
does not push aside שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר — אִין, בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the key inference from the source cited in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That different places followed different rulings on a שבת question
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about רבי אליעזר's town, together with רבי עקיבא's general rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's town and רבי עקיבא's town acted differently on a שבת question, which seems to be forbidden splitting.

steps.title: Why is this a problem? Different places are allowed to differ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this source would be a refutation at all. Different places may have different practices.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what kind of refutation is this? Different places are different!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against using this source as a problem for לא תתגודדו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone already agreed that two separate towns may follow different rulings. Since רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא each had his own town, nothing here breaks לא תתגודדו.

phrases.english: And what kind of refutation is this?
Different places are different!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי מַאי תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea that the source from steps 13 and 14 creates any difficulty.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא as a refutation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא describes two different places, and different places may legitimately differ.

steps.title: Why was the question asked in the first place?
steps.stepSummary: If it is so obvious that different places may differ, the גמרא asks what the person who raised this source was thinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who raised it, why did he raise it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what made someone think this source was a problem. This sets up the next step, which explains his thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not want to throw away a question without understanding it. It looks for a reasonable idea that could have stood behind the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises it as a question or challenge

phrases.english: And the one who raised it,
why did he raise it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקָאָרֵי לַהּ מַאי קָאָרֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up the rejection by asking what the original reasoning was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reasoning led someone to see the ברייתא as a refutation

steps.title: Because שבת is so serious, we might have thought all places count as one
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought that שבת is so strict that the whole world counts as one place, so different towns could not differ. The ברייתא teaches that even on שבת, different places may follow different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that because of the strictness of שבת, it is like one single place. So the ברייתא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the thinking behind the question. Someone could have thought שבת is an exception where all places must act the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that separate towns may differ could have seemed to apply only to lighter matters. The ברייתא shows that this holds even for שבת. So the ברייתא is not a refutation; it teaches something new.
steps.whatToRemember: Different towns may follow different rabbis' rulings, and this holds even for serious matters like שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the reach of לא תתגודדו: local differences between towns are allowed even in the most serious areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: You might have thought
that because of the strictness of שבת
it is like one single place;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא מִשּׁוּם חוּמְרָא דְשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We might have thought that the seriousness of שבת makes all places count as one, so the ברייתא teaches that even on שבת different places may differ.

steps.title: רבי אבהו followed each local rabbi about moving a lamp
steps.stepSummary: A new source: רבי אבהו moved a lamp on שבת in רבי יהושע בן לוי's town, but not in רבי יוחנן's town.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: when רבי אבהו came to the place of רבי יהושע בן לוי, he would move a lamp. And when he came to the place of רבי יוחנן, he would not move a lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another story showing that different places followed different practices on a שבת question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו changed what he did based on whose town he was in. This shows that each place followed its own rabbi, even about שבת.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that Rabbi Abahu, when he happened to come
to the place of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
would move a lamp.
phrases.notes: This is about moving a lamp on שבת. He followed the practice of whichever rabbi's town he was in.

phrases.english: But when he happened to come to the place of Rabbi Yochanan,
he would not move a lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ כִּי אִיקְּלַע לְאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second source about different places acting differently on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: That different towns follow their own rabbi's rulings even on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי אבהו visiting the towns of רבי יהושע בן לוי and רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Practices about moving a lamp on שבת differed from town to town, and even one person acted differently in each.

steps.title: Why is the lamp story a problem at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the story of רבי אבהו and the lamp would be a difficulty, since we already said different places can follow different rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty here? Didn't we already say that different places are different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the source just brought about רבי אבהו and the lamp. We already learned that different towns may follow different rulings, so what is the problem?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 15-17 the גמרא established that even on שבת, different places may follow different rulings. So a story where a lamp is moved in one town but not in another seems to prove nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Different places are different, so each town may follow its own rabbi

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty in this?
Didn't we say that different places are different?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי מַאי קוּשְׁיָא? וְלָא אָמְרִינַן מְקוֹמוֹת שָׁאנֵי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the source in step 18 is a real difficulty, given the principle from step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the lamp story as a proof, since it seems to show only that towns differ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Towns differing was already accepted in step 17, so the story adds nothing.

steps.title: The real question is about רבי אבהו himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the problem is not about towns. It is about one person, רבי אבהו, acting one way here and another way there.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we mean: how could רבי אבהו himself act one way here and a different way there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies what was really bothering it. The question is how a single person could change his own behavior from town to town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different towns following different rabbis is fine. But רבי אבהו is one person with one opinion, so he should either move the lamp everywhere or nowhere. His switching back and forth is the real difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we are saying (clarifying the real point)
How could he act / how did he do

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is going back on 'different places are different.' It accepts that, and now asks a new question about one person's personal behavior.

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ, הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכָא הָכִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu, how could he act this way here,
and how could he act that way there?
phrases.notes: The same word הָכָא is used twice. The first means רבי יהושע בן לוי's town and the second means רבי יוחנן's town.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן הָכִי קָאָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by restating the difficulty in a sharper form.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's own behavior in the two towns
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One person holds one opinion, so acting differently in different towns looks inconsistent.

steps.title: He held back out of respect for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו held like רבי יהושע בן לוי. But in רבי יוחנן's town he did not move the lamp, out of respect for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו held like רבי יהושע בן לוי. When he came to רבי יוחנן's town, he did not move it, out of respect for רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רבי אבהו's real opinion was to allow moving the lamp. In רבי יוחנן's town he held back to honor the local rabbi.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His opinion never changed. Only his behavior changed, out of respect for the rabbi who was in charge of that town. So he was not being inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: His place, the town where he is the rabbi
Moves or carries an object (on שבת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of respect: when you are in another rabbi's town, you avoid openly acting against his rulings.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu holds like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
and when he happened to come to Rabbi Yochanan's place,
he would not move it
out of respect for Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating his real opinion from his outward behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבהו's acting differently in two towns looks like he had no fixed opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: He held like רבי יהושע בן לוי, and held back in רבי יוחנן's town only out of respect.

steps.title: But what about his attendant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי אבהו had an attendant who saw him move the lamp, and might wrongly do the same in רבי יוחנן's town.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the attendant!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the answer. רבי אבהו's attendant saw him move the lamp in one town and might copy him in רבי יוחנן's town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if רבי אבהו himself held back, his attendant could carry on the lenient practice in the wrong place. That would still disrespect רבי יוחנן, or teach the attendant the wrong thing.

phrases.english: But there is the attendant!
phrases.notes: The worry is that the attendant saw רבי אבהו move it elsewhere and might move it here too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא שַׁמָּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that holding back out of respect fully solves the problem
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attendant who saw the lenient practice may repeat it in רבי יוחנן's town.

steps.title: He explained it to the attendant
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו would tell his attendant the reason for the change, so the attendant would not get confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would inform the attendant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אבהו explained the situation to his attendant. That way the attendant knew not to move it in רבי יוחנן's town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the attendant knows the reason, he understands that the lenient practice belongs to one town only. So there is no risk he will copy it in the wrong place.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו held like רבי יהושע בן לוי, held back in רבי יוחנן's town out of respect, and explained this to his attendant. So one person can act differently in different towns without being inconsistent.

phrases.english: That he would inform the attendant.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמוֹדַע לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge about the attendant from step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The attendant would copy the lenient practice in the wrong town.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אבהו told the attendant the reason, so there was no confusion.

steps.title: A new source: they still married each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: although בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreed, they did not refuse to marry women from each other's families.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: although these forbid and those permit, בית שמאי did not hold back from marrying women from בית הלל, and בית הלל did not hold back from marrying women from בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test whether בית שמאי actually acted on their rulings. This step only presents the source; the next step shows why it matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי and בית הלל disagreed about which women were allowed to marry, so each side might view some of the other side's marriages as forbidden. Still, the משנה says they married into each other's families.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵלּוּ אוֹסְרִים וְאֵלּוּ מַתִּירִים —
phrases.english: Although these forbid and those permit —
phrases.notes: This is about the disagreement over whether a צרה (a co-wife) may or must marry the brother-in-law.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai did not hold back
from marrying women from Beit Hillel,
nor Beit Hillel from Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵלּוּ אוֹסְרִים וְאֵלּוּ מַתִּירִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main question of whether בית שמאי acted on their rulings, using a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether בית שמאי actually acted on their own rulings
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה stating that בית שמאי and בית הלל married into each other's families

steps.title: If they acted on their rulings, why marry each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues: if בית שמאי did not act on their rulings, marrying each other makes sense. But if they did act on them, why didn't they hold back?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they did not act on their rulings; that is why they did not hold back. But if you say they did act on them, why didn't they hold back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the משנה challenges the view that בית שמאי acted on their rulings. If they did, marriages between the groups should have been a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי never actually acted on their view, there was only one practice, so there was no problem. But if they did act on it, each side would see some of the other's marriages as forbidden. So why would they marry each other?

phrases.english: It works well if you say they did not act on their view,
that is why they did not hold back.
But if you say they did act on it,
why did they not hold back?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לֹא עָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the source quoted in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that בית שמאי acted on their rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acting on different rulings would make some of each side's marriages forbidden in the other's eyes, yet they married each other.

steps.title: בית שמאי marrying from בית הלל is understandable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to sharpen the question. בית שמאי could marry from בית הלל, because those children would come only from a regular לאו, which does not make them ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that בית שמאי did not hold back from marrying into בית הלל, because those children come from a union forbidden only by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants the easier half of the question first. This sets up the harder half about בית הלל marrying from בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בית שמאי's view, a צרה who married someone else without יבום or חליצה broke only a regular לאו. Breaking a regular לאו does not make the children ממזרים. So בית שמאי had no reason to avoid marrying from בית הלל, and the real problem must be on the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: People who break a regular negative command, one without כָּרֵת

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the answer to the question. The גמרא is only granting one side so it can focus the difficulty on the other side.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מִבֵּית הִלֵּל לֹא נִמְנְעוּ,
phrases.english: It makes sense that Beit Shammai did not hold back from Beit Hillel,
since they are children of those who broke a regular prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מִבֵּית הִלֵּל לֹא נִמְנְעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge from step 25 by granting the easier side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that בית שמאי acted on their rulings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grants that בית שמאי marrying from בית הלל is fine (only a לאו), to set up the harder case of בית הלל marrying from בית שמאי.

steps.title: How could בית הלל marry from בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The other side of the question: by בית הלל's view, children of צרות who married the יבם are from a כרת union and are ממזרים, so how could בית הלל marry into בית שמאי families?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why did בית הלל not hold back from marrying into בית שמאי families? The children of people liable to כרת are ממזרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question it started in step 26. Marrying in one direction was fine, but marrying in the other direction looks like a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allowed a צרה to marry the יבם, but בית הלל held she is still forbidden as a brother's wife, which carries כרת. So by בית הלל's view, children from such a marriage are ממזרים, and בית הלל should have avoided marrying into those families.

keyTerms.meaning: those whose forbidden union carries the punishment of כרת

phrases.english: But בית הלל, from בית שמאי,
why did they not hold back?
The children of those liable to כרת,
phrases.notes: He means the children born when a צרה married the יבם, which בית הלל see as a forbidden brother's wife.

phrases.english: aren't they ממזרים?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל מִבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אַמַּאי לֹא נִמְנְעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the sharpened question begun in step 26 by turning to the problem direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that בית שמאי acted on their ruling, given that the two schools still married each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If בית שמאי acted, some of their families would have children that בית הלל consider ממזרים, so בית הלל should have refused to marry them.

steps.title: Suggested defense: maybe כרת does not make a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way out: maybe בית הלל hold that a child from a כרת union is not a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that בית הלל hold that a ממזר does not come from those liable to כרת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to its own question. This sets up the next step, where the answer will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a union punished by מיתת בית דין makes a ממזר, then the children of the צרות would not be ממזרים even by בית הלל's view. Then בית הלל could marry them with no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say (introduces a suggested answer)

phrases.english: And if you would say
that בית הלל hold
that there is no ממזר from those liable to כרת

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא קָסָבְרִי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense against the question of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the law: narrowing who counts as a ממזר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Children of a כרת union are ממזרים, so בית הלל could not marry them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps בית הלל hold only unions punished by death make a ממזר, so there is no problem.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: both schools agree כרת makes a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The defense is rejected. רבי אלעזר said both schools agree that a ממזר comes from an ערוה union punished by כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר said: even though בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about צרות, they agree that a ממזר comes only from a union whose prohibition is an ערוה prohibition punished by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggested defense from step 28 by quoting רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says both schools agree that an ערוה union with כרת is enough to make a ממזר. So בית הלל cannot say the children of the צרות are fine, and the question of step 27 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: co-wives (rival wives) of the forbidden relative

steps.confusionAlert: The word אֶלָּא here means 'only' (a ממזר comes ONLY from such a union). It does not mean 'rather'. Read it as setting the minimum needed: ערוה with כרת is already enough.

phrases.english: But didn't רבי אלעזר say:
Even though they disagreed,
בית שמאי and בית הלל, about צרות,
they agree that there is no ממזר
except from one whose prohibition is an ערוה prohibition
and is punished by כרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that בית הלל hold a כרת union does not make a ממזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אלעזר reports that both schools agree an ערוה union with כרת does make a ממזר.

steps.title: Proposed proof: בית שמאי did not act on their view
steps.stepSummary: Since there is no other way out, the גמרא suggests proving that בית שמאי never actually acted on their ruling about צרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it right to learn from this that they did not act on their view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion the whole question was building toward: בית שמאי must not have acted on their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית שמאי never let a צרה marry the יבם, there were no problem children, and both sides could marry freely. That would explain the משנה, but the גמרא is about to push back.

keyTerms.meaning: they did not act (on their ruling)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this:
they did not act!
phrases.notes: He means בית שמאי did not actually let a צרה marry the יבם in practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לֹא עָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference that the question of steps 25-29 was pushing toward.
steps.raayaObject: That בית שמאי did not act on their ruling about צרות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that the schools married each other, together with רבי אלעזר's statement that כרת makes a ממזר.

steps.title: No: they did act, but they told each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. בית שמאי did act, but they would tell בית הלל which families had a problem, and בית הלל would stay away from those matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really they did act. They would inform them, and they would keep away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 30 and gives a different way to explain how the schools still married each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two schools could marry each other in general because בית שמאי would warn בית הלל about any family with children of a צרה. בית הלל would then avoid just those matches, so no one married someone forbidden by their own view.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי did act on their view about צרות. Families still married across the schools because they told each other where the problems were.

phrases.english: No, really they did act,
for they would inform them, and they would keep away.
phrases.notes: בית שמאי told בית הלל about the problem families, and בית הלל kept away from those particular matches.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם עָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 30 by offering another explanation of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that בית שמאי did not act on their ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed marrying each other required no problem cases at all. In fact, informing each other let them avoid the problem cases.

steps.title: Support from the purity clause in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports this answer from the end of the משנה: even where one school ruled something pure and the other impure, they still prepared pure items together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this also makes sense, because the end of the משנה teaches: in all the cases of purity and impurity, where these ruled pure and those ruled impure, they did not hold back from preparing pure items with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for step 31 from the last part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טהרות, the schools could only work together if each side said which items it held were impure, and the other side kept away from them. The same kind of informing explains how they could marry each other.
